newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steadies after Buba repo drain.
newsitem.headline: German call money steadies after Buba repo drain.

text.p: German call money rates traded at 3.05/3.10 percent on Wednesday, recovering from levels as low as 3.00 percent on Tuesday after the Bundesbank drained 2.2 billion marks from the market in its weekly tender operation.
Traders said the Bundesbank action removed some of the excess liquity in the market after banks made considerable headway in meeting monthly reserve requirements.
"The Bundesbank had to take some funds out of the market," said one Frankfurt dealer. "Otherwise we would have seen rates today at 3.00 percent."
Banks held 42.6 billion marks in reserves at the German central bank on Tuesday, down from 43.2 billion marks on Monday.
The monthly average fell to 43.2 billion marks from 43.5 billion marks, while Lombard borrowings were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= on Wednesday was lower at 3.10200 percent from Tuesday's level at 3.10633 percent.
